## Statute
§3306(a)(2)(B)

## Reasoning
Section 3306(a)(2)(B) defines an "employer" for agricultural labor as any person who, on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed at least 5 individuals in agricultural labor for some portion of the day.

Applying the facts:
- Jan 24: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, Fred) - Week 4
- Feb 4: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, Fred) - Week 5
- Mar 3: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, Fred) - Week 9
- Mar 18: 5 workers (Cameron, Dan, Emily, Fred, George) - Week 11

- May 9: 5 workers (Cameron, Dan, Emily, Fred, George) - Week 19
- Oct 14: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, George) - Week 41

- Nov 8: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Emily, Fred, George) - Week 45
- Nov 22: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, Fred) - Week 47
- Dec 1: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, George) - Week 48
- Dec 2: 5 workers (Bob, Cameron, Dan, Emily, George) - Week 48

Alice employed at least 5 individuals on 12 different days spanning 11 different calendar weeks. This satisfies the requirement of 10 days in different calendar weeks with at least 5 employees each.

Therefore, Alice meets the definition of "employer" under §3306(a)(2)(B) for agricultural labor in 2017.

## Answer
Answer: Entailment

§3306. Definitions

(a) Employer

    (1) In general

    The term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who-

        (A) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages of $1,500 or more, or

        (B) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or during the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed at least one individual in employment for some portion of the day.

    For purposes of this paragraph, there shall not be taken into account any wages paid to, or employment of, an employee performing domestic services referred to in paragraph (3).

    (2) Agricultural labor

    In the case of agricultural labor, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who-

        (A) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages of $20,000 or more for agricultural labor, or

        (B) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or during the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed at least 5 individuals in employment in agricultural labor for some portion of the day.

    (3) Domestic service

    In the case of domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages in cash of $1,000 or more for such service.

    (datetime.date(2017, 5, 9), ["Cameron", "Dan", "Emily", "Fred", "George"]),
    (datetime.date(2017, 10, 14), ["Bob", "Cameron", "Dan", "Emily", "George"]),
    (datetime.date(2017, 10, 25), ["Bob", "Cameron", "Dan", "Emily", "Fred", "George"]),

    (datetime.date(2017, 11, 22), ["Bob", "Cameron", "Dan", "Emily", "Fred"]),
    (datetime.date(2017, 12, 1), ["Bob", "Cameron", "Dan", "Emily", "George"]),
    (datetime.date(2017, 12, 2), ["Bob", "Cameron", "Dan", "Emily", "George"]),
]

print("Date Analysis:")
print("="*60)

week_numbers = set()
days_with_5_plus = []

for date, workers in dates_and_workers:
    weekday = date.weekday()  # Monday=0, Sunday=6
    # ISO week number (Monday as first day of week)
    iso_week = date.isocalendar()[1]
    year = date.isocalendar()[0]
    workers_count = len(workers)
    
    week_str = f"Jan 24, 2017 (Wk 4)"
    if date.month == 2:
        week_str = "Feb 4, 2017 (Wk 6)"
    elif date.month == 3:
        if date.day == 3:
            week_str = "Mar 3, 2017 (Wk 9)"
        else:
            week_str = "Mar 18, 2017 (Wk 11)"
    elif date.month == 4:
        week_str = "Apr 1, 2017 (Wk 13)"
    elif date.month == 5:
        week_str = "May 9, 2017 (Wk 19)"
    elif date.month == 10:
        if date.day == 14:
            week_str = "Oct 14, 2017 (Wk 42)"
        else:
            week_str = "Oct 25, 2017 (Wk 43)"
    elif date.month == 11:
        if date.day == 8:
            week_str = "Nov 8, 2017 (Wk 45)"
        else:
            week_str = "Nov 22, 2017 (Wk 47)"
    elif date.month == 12:
        if date.day == 1:
            week_str = "Dec 1, 2017 (Wk 48)"
        else:
            week_str = "Dec 2, 2017 (Wk 48)"
    
    print(f"{week_str} | {workers_count} workers | ISO Week {iso_week}")
    
    if workers_count >= 5:
        days_with_5_plus.append(date)
        week_numbers.add((year, iso_week))

print("\n" + "="*60)
print(f"Days with 5+ workers: {len(days_with_5_plus)}")
print(f"Distinct calendar weeks (ISO): {len(week_numbers)}")
print(f"Weeks: {sorted(week_numbers)}")

# Check if at least 10 days in different calendar weeks
if len(days_with_5_plus) >= 10 and len(week_numbers) >= 10:
    print("\n§3306(a)(2)(B) SATISFIED: 10+ days in different weeks with 5+ workers")
else:
    print(f"\n§3306(a)(2)(B) NOT SATISFIED: Need 10 days, got {len(days_with_5_plus)} days in {len(week_numbers)} weeks")
